### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://streamzippy.cyou/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstreamzippy.cyou%2F)

### Comment
> False positive: AdGuard DNS Default server (94.140.14.14) answers 94.140.14.33 (block page, type "safebrowsing") for 128 domains that I operate. The Non-filtering server (94.140.14.140) and all other public resolvers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9) answer normally with Cloudflare IPs. See the attached screenshots.
> 
> The domains are ad-supported movie/TV information and streaming sites of one project (TMDB-based catalogue pages with embedded third-party players), all served through Cloudflare from one origin. They do not contain malware, phishing, scams, cryptojacking or downloads.
> 
> All 128 were registered together on 2026-10-23 as brand/mirror names with a common naming pattern (flix*.cyou and stream*.cyou). I believe this bulk pattern is what caused the classification: the older domains of the same project on the same origin (for example 123chilltv.cyou, moviesubtitles.click) are not blocked, and none of the 128 appears in URLhaus, OpenPhish, Phishing Army, Red Flag Domains or the NRD lists. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance is the first-party "Cookie-Einstellungen" consent modal (dialog#⁠portuna_info, a modal <⁠dialog⁠> with a dark :⁠:⁠backdrop) that dims and gates the Ottendorf-Okrilla municipal homepage, and no existing filter rule covered it. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule ottendorf-okrilla.de#⁠#⁠dialog#⁠portuna_info verified in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, removing the dialog and its dimming with page integrity intact. ## Rule `ottendorf-okrilla.de##dialog#portuna_info` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance on a German municipal site, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle; none of the policy's closing rules apply — it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall (the page shows a consent request, not a request to disable an ad blocker). The simplest fix that works is element hiding of the site's own consent dialog, verified live with the page intact, so no scriptlet or network rule is needed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a4d6e6b97324087978511e7a851f95deb96d2fa6/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
